results.reasoning: Driven at dc47aa5 with node bin/walkdown.js on scratch machines (mktemp HOME and WALKDOWN_HOME under /tmp/judge12-*). No server was needed. The base steps hold (base.txt). A home's path registers that blueprint alone and names its ID and project. Re-importing it says 'already listed' and leaves the registry byte-identical. With no terminal, the repository's path lists billing, checkout and search, marks checkout as already listed, exits 2 and writes nothing. An unknown --only name is refused, and an empty or plain folder says nothing there is a blueprint. Under a real pty (picker.txt), the picker now takes folder names in any letter case ('SEARCH', 'reports' for 0004-Reports) as well as numbers, and a listed folder chosen by name is reported as already listed. The n-0545 fix holds where the sibling stands at a new path (moves.txt C1): a template sibling with no remote gets its own row, and the real alpha keeps its ID when restored elsewhere. Moves, forks with upstream over an ssh port, a local-only row, n-0544's sibling with another origin, worktrees registered or not, a home only a worktree holds, symlinks, letter case and a deepened shallow clone all still behave (moves.txt, regress.txt), and the rule's 19 tagged unit tests and the import CLI scenarios pass. The same harm is still reachable through the old path (s1b.txt, oldpath.txt S1/S2). An agency clones its starter into ~/clients/site for acme (origin acme/site), imports it, and moves it to ~/archive/acme-site. It then clones the same starter into ~/clients/site for zed (origin zed/site). Importing acme's real checkout is refused because label `site` is taken, `--project site` is refused the same way with no keeps-its-IDs hint, and importing zed's checkout reports its home as already listed as acme's 0001-st-web. checkoutGone treats the old path as still standing because the first commit is there, and never asks whether the origin there names the row's origin. That is the test n-0544 and n-0545 apply to a candidate at a new path. The row knew acme/site, and zed's checkout has no remote naming it, so by the fix's own test it is not the same repository. The same happens when the sibling at the old path has no remote at all (S2). It is not one of the accepted ambiguous cases: the row has its first commit and origin, the two clones name different origins, and --project with the right label does not resolve it.
